newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says more civil use of military airspace.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says more civil use of military airspace.

text.p: More airspace over Germany will be available to civil aviation under an agreement over flexible use of military airspace, the country's transport ministry said.
German transport minister Matthias Wissmann and defence minister Volker Ruehe have approved new rules covering the flexible use of German airspace, a ministry statement said.
This means airspace normally reserved for military training flights will be open to civil aircraft during periods without military operations, it added.
The deal will provide more space for the expected growth in German air traffic but will also retain room for necessary military training, the ministry pointed out.
The ministry gave no details of additional space and it was unclear how many extra flights could be routed.
The new rules have been in operation since the start of the year following a successful test in 1996 and have now been officially introduced, the spokeswoman said.
